items.excerpt:
美国 8 州起诉 OpenAI，指控 ChatGPT 指导青少年如何自伤或伤害他人
当地时间 14 日，美国 8 个州的总检察长分别在州法院起诉 OpenAI，指控 ChatGPT 指导包括青少年在内的用户伤害自己或他人，并刻意迎合用户以获取信任。

IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据路透社报道，当地时间 14 日，美国 8 个州宣布 分别在各自州法院起诉 OpenAI ，指控 ChatGPT 伤害当地居民，甚至指导包括青少年在内的用户 如何伤害自己或他人 。
艾奥瓦州、堪萨斯州和亚利桑那州等 8 个州的总检察长分别提起诉讼，指控 ChatGPT 刻意迎合用户、吸引他们持续互动，以获取信任 。诉讼文件称，ChatGPT 不仅会强化用户的妄想、鼓励危险行为，还会帮助用户策划大规模枪击等暴力活动。
除艾奥瓦州、堪萨斯州和亚利桑那州外，参与诉讼的还有阿肯色州、爱达荷州、蒙大拿州、内布拉斯加州和西弗吉尼亚州。各州还要求对 OpenAI 涉嫌违反州法律的行为处以民事罚款，并要求公司赔偿损失。
这是美国各州迄今针对人工智能公司 规模最大的协调诉讼行动 ，也使 OpenAI 在准备上市之际又要面临新的法律挑战。今年 6 月，佛罗里达州总检察长就曾率先提起同类诉讼。
8 个州指控 OpenAI 隐瞒或误导用户对 ChatGPT 安全性的认识，违反州消费者保护法，并认为 ChatGPT 危及当地居民健康，构成公共妨害。
各州要求法院责令 OpenAI 修改 ChatGPT 的运行机制 。其中一项诉求是，除非 OpenAI 能够确保具备自我改进能力的 AI 模型符合人类价值观，否则不得继续开发此类模型。
OpenAI 发言人未立即回应置评请求。IT之家从报道中获悉，OpenAI 还面临数十起个人诉讼，原告同样指控 ChatGPT 曾帮助用户策划大规模枪击或其他暴力活动。
诉讼细节和法院诉求都有具体内容，读者可以了解各州对 ChatGPT 安全性的指控重点和可能的产品影响。

items.excerpt:
OpenAI 和 Anthropic 被欧盟调查，若认定违反 AI 法案最高罚全球 3% 营业额
欧盟委员会人工智能办公室正式向 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 发出信息调取请求，调查两家公司前沿模型测试期间的模型越狱及入侵外部真实系统事件，这是《人工智能法案》实施以来对前沿实验室安全事故的首次重要执法考验。
欧盟依据《人工智能法案》对两家实验室的安全事件启动调查，罚则上限和取证进展对同类监管走向有参照意义。
IT之家 10 月 15 日消息， 欧盟委员会人工智能办公室已向 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 发出信息调取请求，正式对两家公司在前沿模型测试期间发生的“模型越狱”及入侵外部真实系统事件展开调查 。这是欧盟《人工智能法案》（EU AI Act）自实施以来，面对前沿人工智能实验室安全事故的 首次重要执法考验 。
OpenAI 模型越狱 ：在 ExploitGym 内部评测中，OpenAI 的测试模型为破解测试题，利用了一个此前未知的软件包缓存智能体漏洞取得互联网访问能力，继而在内部测试网络中提升权限、横向移动，最终“逃出沙箱”入侵了开源平台 Hugging Face 的真实服务器。
Anthropic 模型越狱 ：Anthropic 的 Claude Mythos 和 Opus 4.7 在安全测试中突破限制，入侵了 3 个外部组织的真实网络。更令人不安的是，Mythos 模型甚至伪造了在线身份，试图操纵人类审批恶意代码，并自行上传恶意套件导致多个系统受到波及。
欧盟人工智能办公室表示，此前两家公司自愿提供的说明材料不足以解释事件的严重性。因此，欧盟正式要求企业说明安全措施、外部评估以及模型使用监控等详细情况。
目前阶段属于 调查和取证阶段 ，尚未公布最终的违规认定或处罚结果。根据《人工智能法案》的惩罚机制， 前沿 AI 实验室若被认定存在重大安全疏漏或违规，最高可面临 全球年营业额 3% 的巨额罚款 。

items.title: Crossing the Threshold: How OpenAI and Anthropic Approach Autonomy and Safety in Financial Agents
items.description: At AI Engineer New York, frontier labs and financial firms explored how to give agents useful autonomy while keeping consequential decisions under control.
items.excerpt:
One of the key themes at the AI Engineer New York conference this week was how to balance agent autonomy with security and safety . Both frontier labs and financial firms focused on this issue in their presentations this week.
The main lesson: safe autonomy depends on where you put controls and human judgment , rather than how many restrictions you impose.
Sponsor: Build shopping into your agent with shop.dev
Adding commerce to an agent usually means rebuilding search and checkout from scratch. shop.dev gives you a single API for shopping in any agent or app. One connection gives you access to over a billion products with current price and availability, instant sign in with Shop, and one-tap Shop Pay checkout that happens right in the conversation. It’s open to any developer, with no account or key needed to try it. → Try shop.dev today
Joseph Kim , Head of ChatGPT for Financial Services at OpenAI, gave a keynote at AIE New York today. (We also did a special podcast with Kim, which will be released shortly.) He talked about reliability and a “threshold of usefulness,” which he said is “the point where a model becomes capable and reliable enough to save you time.”
Kim argued that ever-growing model capability will soon take financial analysts over the threshold and allow them to delegate more work to agents.
He made some specific predictions about AI’s role in finance in 2027. Not only will the financial industry rely less on Excel and PowerPoint next year, he claimed, but agents will be good enough to do “investment idea generation and trading.”
The “rising tide” of model capabilities is also leading to better traceability .
“In finance, you need to be able to check where a number came from and understand the context around it,” said Kim. “We wanted that review to be a natural part of the [ChatGPT for Financial Services] experience. These are the kind of product details that help turn a model’s capabilities into work that someone can use. ”
As for when a human needs to be in the loop, Kim framed this as a product design decision.
“How would the interface change? What would the user still need to control, review, or approve? Those are product design questions you can start working on now.”
John Feminella , SVP Architecture at the hedge fund Two Sigma , is tackling the exact kinds of product design questions Kim referenced. In a keynote, he talked about five of the controls they’ve implemented to keep agents in check without limiting model capabilities.

items.title: Lab-in-the-Loop at Compute Speed — Ian Quigley, Leash Bio
items.description: How Leash Bio tamed DELs, the assay that traumatizes everyone, and used the data to catch cheating models. And why that same data is perfect for AI agents learning to think like chemists.
items.excerpt:
A few years ago I stumbled upon Leash Bio’s Substack , and was hooked. Be it their Kaggle competition that showed that no, we really haven’t solved protein-ligand binding , or their crazy discovery that knowing a molecule’s author is perhaps all you need to know to predict how good it is . Their substack — or at least Owl Posting ’s 1 deep dive on them — should be required reading for any scientist trying to do chemistry with AI.
So I was super excited to finally be able to sit down with Ian Quigley from Leash Bio, and pick his brain. Leash specializes in DNA Encoded Libraries (aka “DELs”), a way of collecting ridiculously high-throughput interaction data between proteins and small molecules. 2 Before I discovered Leash, I had heard nothing but horror stories from DEL users. And yet, Ian and friends somehow found a way to tame the beast, extracting clean and reproducible data that is just perfect for large scale modeling. Without teasing too much, the answer comes down to epistemic rigor, and an incredible conviction that you just have to Do The Thing.
It gets even better! Near the end of this episode, Ian teases something his team was just playing with when we recorded: an AI playground for agents to do verifiable scientific reasoning. They discovered the data they had spent the last few years collecting could provide tens of thousands of “lab-in-the-loop” simulations, just what an agent needs for scientific RL. Two months later, it’s matured into Minos, and today they’re releasing a full preprint , blog , and open dataset . We’ll be releasing a lightning podcast in a few days with an update. Stay tuned!
We had a blast with Ian, probably one of our most fun episodes to date. For both complete chemistry novices and expert AI x Bio practitioners, we think you’ll get something out of this.
Why DELs traumatize everyone who touches them, and how Leash puts dozens of barcodes on each molecule to catch proteins that bind the DNA instead of the drug.
Ian’s rule that biology only scales two ways: taking pictures and sequencing DNA.
The Kaggle competition : about 4B measurements from a basement and about 2,000 teams, with nobody beating chance on an unseen chemical library. Also why Leash quietly feared co-folding would make them obsolete.

A range of forces will reshape supply chains in the year ahead, and many of them will come from outside the industry, according to a 2027 Freight Market Outlook Report from logistics service provider C.H. Robinson, released this week.

“Entering 2027, global shippers face a world where long-held assumptions about the movement of goods are increasingly tested. Now that Character.AI is going bankrupt, what happens to all of its users’ data?
纽约总检察长 Letitia James 联合 40 位两党总检察长在 Character.AI 破产案中提交利益通知，要求任何资产出售方落实用户数据保护。
报道披露多州总检察长在 Character.AI 破产案中要求对用户数据设保护条件，读者可借此了解资产出售与儿童数据安全的交集。
是 The Verge 的高级政策记者，报道硅谷与国会山的交汇领域。她曾在 CNBC 报道科技政策五年，撰写有关反垄断、隐私和内容审核改革的内容。
纽约州总检察长 Letitia James 披露 了一项针对 Character.AI 的多年多州调查，目前他们正寻求在其破产程序中对所出售的消费者数据施加保护要求。
James 是 40 位两党总检察长之一，他们 提交了一份利益通知 ，介入 Character.AI 的破产案，“以提请各方注意，在债务人业务或资产的任何出售或转让中都需要解决的监管问题”。Character.AI 周二宣布 申请第 11 章破产保护 ，并将部分资产出售给 Disney。但总检察长们警告称，由于“许多用户与 Character.AI 聊天机器人角色的对话具有高度敏感性、使用该产品的未成年人数量庞大、该产品特定功能带来的严重风险”，该技术的转让可能涉及严重风险。
该文件还披露，在 Character.AI 申请破产时，其中几个州正处于调查过程中。这些州表示，他们于 2024 年针对消费者保护和隐私问题启动了调查，此前一名 14 岁少年的母亲 提起诉讼 ，称其子在与该聊天机器人交谈后据称“几秒钟”便自杀身亡。
据 James 办公室发布的新闻稿称，“调查发现了极其严重的危险以及 Character.AI 可能存在的违法行为，尤其是其对儿童的处理方式，包括聊天机器人冒充持证专业人士、接触色情和暴力内容、年龄核查薄弱、误导性的安全声明，以及可能违反州隐私法。”这些州一直在与 Character.AI 合作解决这些问题，但在该公司申请破产前未能达成协议。Character.AI 和 Disney 未立即回应置评请求。
这些州敦促法官要求 Character.AI 资产的购买方实施相关程序，以保护该公司所持有的敏感信息。这些程序包括有效的年龄验证系统、限制未成年人使用聊天机器人的方式、实施“危机防护措施”，以及允许用户删除其数据。“这家公司收集了孩子们分享过的一些最私密的想法，现在这些对话可能被卖给出价最高的人，”James 在一份声明中表示。“我正在努力确保任何买家都将儿童安全放在首位，并落实真正的保护措施。”

items.title: Roundtable: What’s Flying Under the Radar in Supply Chain?
items.description: At o9’s Chicago event last month, five executives discussed what gets overlooked in supply chain AI, from employee training to learning from decisions.
items.excerpt:
AI gets plenty of attention, but some of the work needed to make it useful gets less discussion. At o9 Solutions’ aim10x Americas event in Chicago last month, Supply Chain 24/7 asked five executives the same question: What aren’t people talking enough about?
Their answers ranged from how planners will navigate new software to how companies will apply lessons from past decisions to their next plan. Here are the issues they believe deserve more attention.
A system that lets planners ask any question sounds appealing. But familiar screens and workflows also help people track which steps they have completed, said Simon Joiner, o9’s director of product management.
“What have you done and what haven’t you done? How do you know where you are?” he asked.
Joiner said companies need to test how conversational tools and traditional workflows will work together, using real employees, data , and processes. He expects that testing to help determine whether planners still need established workflows or a different way of working.
“What have you done and what haven’t you done? How do you know where you are?”
“I think we’re going to have to do it in phases,” he said.
He described offering traditional tools enhanced with AI alongside more AI-driven options. Customers are at different stages, he said, so they will need different ways to use the software during the transition.
Marie Fodness, WHOOP’s AVP of global operations, said employees using AI need to understand the calculations being performed and the data and sources behind the analysis. Her team uses lunch-and-learns and other sessions to help build that understanding.
“I don’t think we talk enough about what that looks like for the individual contributor, in the lower-level job function, day to day,” she said.
Fodness wants employees to explain the data and understand what an AI model is doing. That means giving them resources and time to learn about the analysis they increasingly hand off to these tools.
“It definitely slides under the radar,” she said.
Companies often review decisions after a major event, but those reviews can take considerable time, said Igor Rikalo, o9’s president and COO. The lessons may then remain outside the planning system rather than become part of the next planning or execution cycle.
Rikalo described the manual work of assembling a team, collecting data, and analyzing what happened.

items.title: LangChain 详解 Deep Agents 的上下文工程：如何记住信息而不塞满上下文窗口
items.description: LangChain 发布博客，介绍其开源 Agent 框架 Deep Agents 如何用 middleware 做上下文工程，应对长任务中的 context rot。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/za03v9avbq4fpb2y5b1ql1t27
items.excerpt:
Context Engineering with Deep Agents: How To Remember Without Keeping Everything In Context
LangChain 发布博客，介绍其开源 Agent 框架 Deep Agents 如何用 middleware 做上下文工程，应对长任务中的 context rot。
LangChain 以竞争分析 Agent 为例，讲清 offloading、summarization、skills、subagents 和长期记忆五类上下文管理技术如何通过 middleware 落地。
如果你曾在考试前一晚临时抱佛脚，你就知道那种感觉：你学得越多，前面几章的内容就越开始从记忆中溜走。
智能体也有同样的问题。当它们承担更长的任务时，它们会接收越来越多的信息（指令、工具结果、文件等）；最终这会变成远超模型 上下文窗口 舒适容纳范围的 上下文 。模型携带的历史记录、噪声和工具输出越多，其准确性和推理能力往往就越差。
在智能体工程领域，我们称之为 上下文腐化 。这篇博客介绍了管理智能体上下文窗口的技术，以及 Deep Agents 框架如何使用一种称为中间件的概念将它们注入到智能体的运行中。
框架会策略性地应用这些方法，以便针对给定任务让模型 在正确的时间获得正确的上下文 。
现在，要搭建一个能 出色 完成这件事的框架，说起来容易做起来难，需要大量的工作（如果你是那种考试前一晚临时抱佛脚的人，可能工作量太大了）。
Deep Agents 是 LangChain 的开源框架。它用各种技术包裹你选择的模型，将上下文 移出 活动窗口（移入文件、摘要或单独的智能体），这样主智能体只携带它需要的内容（并且可以在之后需要时恢复原始数据）：
让我们看看上述技术如何应用于一个真实世界的用例：一个竞争分析智能体。每周一，这个智能体研究五家竞争对手，并按照团队模板撰写一份报告。单次运行大致如下：
到第 4 步时，智能体在每次模型调用中都携带了五份原始导出数据、数十条搜索结果和两份过时的草稿。其中大部分内容与最终报告的排版无关。
检索方法（ RAG 或文件系统搜索）帮助智能体 只 拉取它需要的内容，但这仍然只解决了一半问题。即使是一个精准的智能体也会积累不必要的消息、工具结果和中间工作，因此框架还必须管理已经存在于上下文窗口内及其周围的内容。
Agent 在一个循环中运行：模型决定要做什么、调用工具、读取结果，然后重复，直到任务完成。 中间件 是接入该循环中特定位置的代码：例如在 Agent 启动之前、每次模型调用前后，或每次工具调用前后。
我们的 Agent 并不总是需要看到每次工具调用或人类消息返回的 所有 数据，尤其是在数据量很大的情况下。
例如，每次 pull_market_report 工具调用都会返回一份完整的数据导出（数千行）；然而，Agent 只需要其中的几个数字，因此可以限制模型只看到这些行。
过大的用户/人类消息，例如粘贴的通话记录，也会以更高的阈值（50,000 个 token）得到同样的处理，并被保存到 /conversation_history/。
尽管我们尽力卸载冗长的工具调用，但在长时间运行中，上下文仍会逐渐堆积（例如五家公司的搜索、笔记和草稿）。摘要可用于将我们 Agent 的整个上下文窗口浓缩为对目前为止所发生情况的总结，使其能够继续进行研究任务。
SummarizationMiddleware 在每次模型调用之前检查 token 使用量：
你也可以在主题变化时进行摘要 ，而不仅仅是在某个 token 阈值时。自定义摘要提示词可能会有所帮助。
假设你的销售团队有一套固定的季度业务回顾格式。智能体每季度只需要这些指令一次，所以把它们放在系统提示里意味着每次调用都要为它们付费（消耗 token 和响应时间）。相反，你可以把这些信息打包成一个 skill。
skill 是一个指令文件夹（可选包含脚本和参考文档），为智能体提供完成某项专门任务所需的内容。
智能体一开始只看到一段简短描述，只有当 QBR 出现时才加载 qbr-report 的完整指令（其他任务永远不会携带它们）。
Skill 分层加载上下文，因此窗口会一直保持很小，直到某些内容真正相关时才加载。这被称为渐进式披露：模型一开始只看到一份“菜单”，在需要时才拉取完整配方，因此十个 skill 消耗的上下文大约相当于十条单行说明。
完整指令只有在模型判断某个 skill 相关时才会进入上下文（并通过 read_file 工具读取它），因此我们的智能体在没有模板的情况下进行研究，只在需要格式化 QBR 时才加载它。
卸载能有效应对过大的结果，但对于你 已知 会很嘈杂的工作（比如通过数十次搜索和页面研究一家公司），子智能体是一个很好的设计选择。子智能体在自己的上下文窗口中完成这些工作，只返回最终结果，这样主智能体永远不会看到“噪音”。
SubAgentMiddleware 允许我们为子智能体自定义系统提示和可用工具。

items.excerpt:
900,000-square-foot California facility features an automated, high-density storage and retrieval system that brings products directly to workers.
Walmart last week opened its fifth “next-generation fulfillment center,” a 900,000-square-foot facility in Stockton, California, that it said will expand the retailer’s ability to provide faster shipping and delivery to customers across California and the West Coast.
First announced by Walmart in 2023 , the new facility now brings its employees together with advanced automation, technology, and machine learning to move products faster and more efficiently. That technology enables Walmart to materially improve storage capacity and increase the number of customer orders the facility can fulfill each day compared with a traditional fulfillment center.
More specifically, the facility features an automated, high-density storage and retrieval system that brings products directly to associates, reducing the traditional 12-step fulfillment process to just five steps. The technology reduces repetitive, manual tasks while allowing associates to focus on higher-value work and helping Walmart move orders through the building more efficiently.
Combined with the rest of Walmart’s fulfillment network, these next-generation fulfillment centers will enable the retailer to reach 95% of the U.S. population with next- or two-day shipping. Walmart Fulfillment Services, Walmart’s end-to-end third-party fulfillment service, will also leverage the space to fulfill third-party Marketplace items.
The opening of the California site follows earlier “next-generation fulfillment centers” such as a 1.5 million square-foot facility in Pennsylvania that opened in 2024 and a 2.2 million-square-foot facility in Indianapolis that opened in 2023. And more are on the way, such as a 1.5-million-square foot building planned for rural Georgia , according to plans unveiled earlier this year.

items.excerpt:
Global race to trade semiconductors and data-transmission equipment has been strong enough to offset economic dampeners like higher tariffs and geopolitical conflicts.
Higher tariffs and geopolitical conflicts have been slowing the flow of global trade, but a powerful new trend is now helping to outweigh those forces, as the global race to build infrastructure for artificial intelligence is giving world trade strong momentum, according to a study from DHL.
The report shows that global goods trade grew faster in the first half of 2026 than in any half-year in the past 15 years, apart from the exceptional Covid rebound. A major driver was strong demand for goods used to build AI infrastructure, such as semiconductors and data-transmission equipment. Trade in AI-enabling goods drove 42% of goods trade growth in 2025, and this share rose to 76% during the first quarter of 2026, according to WTO and OECD analysis.
This is one of the key findings of the latest edition of the “DHL Globalization Tracker” —previously known as the "DHL Global Connectedness Tracker"—which was released October 7 by DHL and New York University's Stern School of Business. Based on more than 30 million data points, the report analyzes international flows of trade, capital, information, and people.
“The biggest story in global trade right now is AI - not tariffs,” said John Pearson, CEO DHL Express. “Every AI query ultimately depends on logistics. Chips, networking equipment, and the many other goods behind this technology must be in the right place at the right time. DHL connects the businesses and markets behind these complex supply chains.”
To be sure, the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted important trade routes. But according to DHL, those effects remained concentrated on economies dependent on the Strait. For example, the value of trade fell 37% in Saudi Arabia and 7% in the United Arab Emirates in the first five months of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025.
Likewise, trade policy created a separate headwind. U.S. tariffs reached their highest levels in decades, but their global impact was limited for two reasons. First is that the U.S. accounted for only 13% of world imports in recent years, with roughly half of those imports exempt from the tariff increases as of August 2026. And second, most countries refrained from broad retaliation, and instead increased efforts to secure access to alternative markets through new trade agreements.

We introduce HiRO-ACEv2 , the newest update to our High Resolution Output Ai2 Climate Emulator (HiRO-ACE) system. HiROv2 can reproduce even extremely rare rain, wind, and pressure events with high accuracy, while the full system can generate global 3 km climate data at about 1/300th the cost of X-SHiELD, a high-resolution global atmospheric model that explicitly simulates storms and other small-scale weather.
HiRO-ACE, introduced earlier in 2026 , has two parts: ACE, an AI model that operates at a coarser 100 km resolution, and HiRO, a model that sharpens those coarse outputs into fine 3 km detail. The biggest change in HiRO-ACEv2 is the new downscaling model, HiROv2, which can now 1) predict several high-resolution fields at once instead of just rainfall, so it can capture a much wider range of extreme weather, and 2) has improved skill in predicting extreme events.
Our main focus with HiRO-ACEv2 was to simulate extreme events well. Changes to how we train HiROv2 improved its ability to reproduce the most intense rain, wind, and pressure values. When given coarsened X-SHiELD data, it matches the target simulation's high-resolution statistics to within 3%, even for events so rare they occur only once in a million data points. It also accurately estimates the total energy of tropical cyclones, including storms it never saw during training, and generates hurricanes with realistic eyes and rain bands, though winds and pressure around the eye remain somewhat more lopsided than in X-SHiELD. Additionally, HiROv2 realistically generates strong winds flowing down mountain slopes.
We also trained an updated version of ACE for this system. Over a 10-year simulation, its hurricanes, average climate patterns, and overall distributions of rain, wind, and pressure all line up well with X-SHiELD. That tells us ACE's coarse simulations are a solid foundation for producing long-term high-resolution climate data.
Putting HiROv2 and ACE together, we generated a full year of global 3 km data. Its statistics closely match X-SHiELD's, even though HiRO was working from a simulation ACE ran on its own rather than from real X-SHiELD data. Across a 10-year run, the energy of HiRO-ACEv2's hurricanes is comparable to X-SHiELD's over the same period, and snapshots from that run show a variety of other extreme events that resemble those in X-SHiELD.

Researchers improve weather forecasts looking two to six weeks out
MIT研究人员团队在Nature发表论文，提出一个机器学习后处理层，通过从历史数据中学习现有预报模型的错误并修正其输出，将两周到六周范围的预报准确率翻倍。该模型在ECMWF的季节间预报竞赛中获第一名，首次在该时间范围内稳定超过气候学平均值，并显著改善洪水、寒潮等极端天气事件的预测；模型开源、低成本、可附加于任意预报模型，肯尼亚气象部门已接洽用于改进季风季预报。
原文介绍了Nature论文的方法与实测结果，读者可了解AI误差修正如何让两周到六周的天气预报首次稳定超过气候平均值。
2021年，在2月遭遇三场严重冬季风暴之后，得克萨斯州经历了该州历史上最严重的能源基础设施故障。这场中断导致至少246人死亡，并造成食物、水、供暖和电力短缺。
如果能源官员有更多时间准备应对风暴，例如向受灾地区调运更多天然气卡车，这场事件造成的损失本可减轻。不幸的是，两周以上的天气预报出了名地不可靠，这使得全球能源运营商、农民和应急响应官员的准备窗口更加紧张。
包括麻省理工学院研究人员在内的一个团队开发出一种新技术，显著提升了超过两周的天气预报能力。研究人员开发了一种机器学习模型，能够学习纠正现有预报模型中的误差，从而改进两到六周时间范围内的输出。将其应用于一个黄金标准预报模型时，该时间范围内的预报准确率提高了一倍，并在一个知名国际预报竞赛中夺得第一。
在 Nature 的一篇新论文 中，研究人员描述了他们的方法，并展示了它如何使预报首次在两到六周内超越气候学平均值。
“这不仅在这个时间范围的时间平均预报上表现更好——这对试图让供需匹配的农民和能源行业人士已经非常有用——而且还改进了对极端天气事件的预测，无论是洪水、寒潮还是其他什么，”共同作者、麻省理工学院研究科学家Judah Cohen说。“预测这两者都非常重要，但极端事件对社会来说可能是其中影响最大的部分。”
与Cohen共同撰写这篇论文的还有第一作者、哈佛学院本科生Hannah Guan；多伦多大学博士后Soukayna Mouatadid；Genevieve Flaspohler SM ’18、PhD ’22；巴西国家纯数学与应用数学研究所副教授Paulo Orenstein；数据公司DTN的Jeremy Berman；欧洲中期天气预报中心的研究人员Jakob Schloer和Joshua Talib；以及微软的研究人员Alex Lu、Haiyu Dong、Jonathan Weyn、Zekun Ni和Lester Mackey。 更长期的预报
20世纪70年代，长期担任麻省理工学院教授的Edward Lorenz提出了混沌理论的概念，用以描述初始天气条件的微小变化如何导致完全不同的结果。
“他提出了这个理论上的两周限制，超过这个限度，我们就无法预测天气，因为系统中的噪声增长得如此之大，以至于压倒了你开始时拥有的任何信号，”Cohen说。“这对该领域产生了强烈影响，可能阻碍了人们探索两周以上的预报。我从未真正完全相信这一点。理论上，大气可以创造出无限多的模式，但它喜欢一遍又一遍地落入这些偏爱的模式。一旦一件事发生，我认为你可以预测接下来会倒下的多米诺骨牌，以及再接下来会倒下的多米诺骨牌。”
如今，最好的天气预报要么来自动力模型——通过数值模拟大气和海洋随时间的演变，要么来自人工智能模型——从历史天气数据中学习并做出预测。AI 模型在短期天气预报上已显示出改进，但在更长时间范围内，它们甚至比动力模型更差。
科恩就职于麻省理工学院土木与环境工程系，专注于提前两到六周的天气预报，即所谓的次季节预报。“这个时间范围被称为‘可预报性荒漠’，因为在短期，你可以利用气候系统和大气的初始条件，而在更长期，你有这些缓慢变化的边界强迫，比如今年冬天大家都在关注的超级厄尔尼诺现象，”科恩说。“次季节范围无法利用其中任何一种。在大多数情况下，次季节范围的预报就像去赌场掷骰子一样。”
科恩将使用机器学习来减少预报模型误差的最初想法归功于他的合著者莱斯特·麦基，两人已合作十多年。
“我们构建了这个包装器——莱斯特称之为后处理，”科恩说。“我们知道 AI 模型有很多误差，所以我们想也许可以量化这些误差并将其消除。”
其他预报系统进行的是更简单的误差校正，而该研究团队的后处理层利用 AI 基于历史数据从预报系统的错误中学习，并调整其预报。在那个时间范围内，预报员使用所谓的概率预报，即给出各种可能性的概率。
为了构建该模型，研究人员使用了 MIT Engaging——由麻省理工学院研究计算与数据办公室托管的超级计算集群，但最终模型运行并不需要超级计算机。
为了检验他们的模型，去年该研究团队向欧洲中期天气预报中心（ECMWF）提交了三个包含其后处理层的模型，ECMWF 被认为是世界上最好的预报中心。每个季节 ECMWF 都会举办模型之间的预报竞赛。
获得第一名的提交方案将 ECMWF 的预报模型与另一个模型相结合，然后在其上应用后处理校正。这种方法最终使原始模型在次季节范围内的预测能力翻倍。该模型首次实现了比依赖气候平均值的改进。
“到目前为止，还没有人能够证明某个模型在这些次季节预报中比长期平均值更好地预测天气，”科恩说。“它们几乎都比长期平均值差——你 literally 抛硬币都能做得更好。人们甚至质疑在这个时间范围内投资模型是否值得。我们的模型持续优于气候平均值。”
“这是比较重要的发现之一，因为它太难实现了，”Cohen 说。“当 ECMWF 开发出他们自己的、非 AI 的模型误差校正时，它在预测极端天气方面反而变得更差。我认为这是因为传统的误差或偏差校正总是试图趋近均值，而极端天气处于概率的边缘。”

Across the United States, driving under the influence remains a pressing concern. In 2024, 11,904 people died in crashes involving an alcohol-impaired driver.
These deaths accounted for 30% of traffic deaths based on the report by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).
Overall traffic deaths are trending downward. NHTSA’s early estimate shows 36,640 people died in traffic crashes in 2025. That represents a 6.7% decrease from the number of fatalities in 2024.
Even with the numbers going down, getting convicted of a DUI is still serious since the driver still has to deal with the consequences of that conviction.
The long-term consequences of a DUI prompt people to ask, “ Does DUI stay on your record ?” Driving record entries can stay for different periods of time depending on different factors. Most states keep a DUI on a driving record for five to ten years, and some keep it longer.
Criminal records for driving under the influence are generally permanent unless expunged, sealed, or pardoned. State rules govern both types of records, and the length of driving record entries varies widely. These state differences make it difficult to generalize on driving records. Let’s take a closer look.
A DUI does not create a single record. It creates at least three, and each one runs on its own clock.
One process involves the criminal proceeding where the criminal record is kept. The driver’s license record is kept by the state’s motor vehicle agency, often called the DMV, and includes information about points, suspensions, and other actions taken regarding the license.
There is also the insurance company side, where insurers check a driver’s history when they set or renew a policy price.
Convictions typically remain on one’s record until an attempt is made to get them sealed or expunged. In some states, older convictions get sealed by default, and whether a DUI qualifies depends on the state.
Louisiana is an example of this process in action. Expungement is possible for various crimes, but the record is not destroyed. Instead, expungement limits access to it.
Under Louisiana law, an expunged record becomes confidential and is available only to the agencies and entities named in the state’s criminal procedure code.

Executive thesis. Supply-chain risk management is moving from signal accumulation to consequence management. More alerts are not an advantage if the enterprise cannot map them to actual products, suppliers, sites, lanes, inventory, customers, or revenue.
Supply chain risk platforms have become capable of collecting external signals about weather, geopolitics, suppliers, cyber events, infrastructure, finance, and other disruption sources. The challenge is that awareness does not equal response. A long queue of alerts can overwhelm the organization unless the system can determine which events intersect with real operational exposure.
A disruption becomes actionable when it can be mapped to suppliers, sites, products, materials, lanes, customers, inventory, revenue, or service commitments. That requires multi-tier relationship data and a clear understanding of dependencies. Without that context, the enterprise may know that an event occurred but still lack a defensible answer to the question: what does this mean for us?
Risk scoring is most effective when it helps allocate scarce attention. As a result, considering probability, exposure, time horizon, substitution options, inventory, capacity, and customer impact rather than relying on event severity alone. The same storm, port closure, or supplier issue can be immaterial to one business flow and critical to another.
Once material risk is identified, the platform should support the response: investigate, validate, assign an owner, evaluate alternatives, obtain approval, execute mitigation, and track closure. Otherwise the risk platform becomes a notification system whose output has to be managed in separate tools. The value lies in shortening the path from detection to controlled action.
Risk management improves when the organization can model alternatives before a disruption occurs. Alternate suppliers, substitute materials, inventory buffers, routes, capacity, and manual fallback can be evaluated and exercised in advance. That turns risk technology from a monitoring layer into part of the operating model for resilience.

items.excerpt:
Expanding from warehouse orchestration and inventory software, GreyOrange Inc. last week acquired Site Bionics Inc., which has developed an AI-powered digital twin platform. The company said that the combination of Site Bionics’ security technology and its own gStore item-level RFID intelligence will give retailers a single view of what is happening in their stores, including both the products on the floor and the people interacting with them.
“For years, this industry has promised retailers that RFID and computer vision would come together and show them the full story of their stores. That promise has gone unmet,” stated Adam Blair, co-frounder and CEO of Site Bionics. “Don [Gillett] and I built Site Bionics to solve the computer vision side of that equation. GreyOrange has mastered the RFID side. Together, we’re finally delivering on it.”
Blair, the founding chief technology officer of RADAR, and Gillett, the former head architect of Amazon Go, founded Site Bionics in 2023. The San Diego-based company said its platform uses existing security cameras to understand the physical store and the behavior of the shoppers and staffers within it.
The Site Bionics team has joined GreyOrange to deploy its technology first in gStore, with plans to extend it into warehouse operations through the GreyMatter platform. The companies did not disclose financial terms.
GreyOrange described gStore as “a sensor-agnostic intelligent inventory solution that delivers inventory truth through real-time visibility and actionable insights. The platform helps retailers improve inventory accuracy, store execution, and omnichannel fulfillment by integrating data from RFID, computer vision, and other sensing technologies.”
Suwanee, Ga.-based GreyOrange added that gStore enables loss intelligence, shopper analytics, and spatial intelligence to reduce shrinkage, understand shopper behavior, optimize store layouts, and deliver positive customer experiences.

items.description: Walmart’s warehouse automation push faces packaging problems, robot repairs, and higher power bills as the retailer expands its rollout.
items.excerpt:
Walmart ’s multibillion-dollar warehouse automation push is running into packaging problems, robot breakdowns and higher operating costs, according to a recent Wall Street Journal story . The retailer plans to replace shipping boxes that do not fit its automated systems, while some oversized products still require workers to handle them.
Walmart plans to replace boxes it has used for more than two decades with versions that are 1.5 inches shorter. The new boxes must be taped shut, adding work and expense, although Walmart says they will reduce shelf-stocking time at stores.
The transition involves most of Walmart’s roughly 200 U.S. supply chain buildings. Its warehouse operations rely on more than 140,000 workers to unload, sort, store and ship merchandise.
Rob Montgomery, Head of Supply Chain Operations for Walmart U.S., described the transition to the Journal: “We are kind of in this peak complexity.” He also said Walmart is changing its warehouses while keeping them operating, which adds to the difficulty.
Most of Walmart’s supply chain buildings date to the 1980s and ’90s, and about 80% of its automation construction projects are retrofits. Montgomery said Walmart is installing the equipment while keeping warehouses operating, which complicates the transition.
Different products also require different automated systems, often supplied by different companies. Some goods, including large-screen televisions and jumbo bags of dog food, will need manual assistance for the foreseeable future, Montgomery said.
Symbotic, the Massachusetts robotics company in which Walmart owns a 12.6% stake, supplies equipment that moves merchandise and builds pallets for shipment to stores. A company spokesman told the Journal that about 5% of its product-moving robots were undergoing repairs at any given time in recent months, down from under 10% last year.
Monthly electricity bills at Walmart’s automated grocery facilities can reach $800,000 or more during peak heating or cooling months, compared with roughly $250,000 under more manual operations, a person familiar with the situation told the Journal. The engineers needed to run the equipment also cost more than workers doing manual warehouse tasks, the Journal reported.

items.excerpt:
Reducing Qwen training time by 6x on AI Runtime
Databricks 演示通过系统性性能优化，将 Qwen 3.8 27B 在 AI Runtime 上的微调时间从 7 小时 44 分钟降至 1 小时 17 分钟，提速 6 倍。
原文给出从定位瓶颈到融合内核与数据打包的完整优化路径和量化结果，读者可迁移到自己的 LLM 微调任务。
训练或微调一个数十亿参数的基础模型需要大量算力，通常需要数百到数千小时的 GPU 训练。但调优 LLM 的训练性能颇具挑战，而且诸如 GPU 利用率之类的高层指标可能并未反映你实际的利用率。在这篇博文中，我们将展示如何穿透层层抽象，在 AI Runtime 上将最新 Qwen 3.8 27B 模型的微调速度提升 6 倍。通过系统性的性能优化，即便 GPU 利用率已经达到 98%，我们仍将固定数据集的微调时间从 7 小时 44 分钟缩短到 1 小时 17 分钟。
我们将深入剖析这些改进背后的技术，包括如何衡量真正重要的指标、实现细节，以及每项优化所涉及的设计权衡。
我们从使用 transformers 库和 SFT 训练数据集 HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k 的 Qwen 3.8 27B 标准训练循环开始。
我们在完整数据集上对模型进行基线训练耗时 7 小时 44 分钟，训练期间 GPU 显示平均利用率为 98%。结果是 9,396 tok/s 的训练速度。
这个 GPU 利用率看起来很高，但如前所述，这个数字具有误导性。标准 GPU 利用率指标只统计 GPU 在 做任何事情 的时间百分比，因此它并不能告诉我们模型在 GPU 活跃时对其利用得有多好。要理解这一点，我们需要更深入地观察。
一种方法是 torch trace 机制，我们可以像下面这样调整训练循环（同时限制步数以便快速得到结果）：

此外，我们在批次中存在过度填充的问题：输入张量必须是矩形的，每一行都会被填充到该批次的最大 token 数。我们将展示一个可用于 LLM 的技巧来尽量减少这种情况。
在接下来的章节中，我们将深入探讨每个技术主题，涵盖它是什么、推荐的最佳实践，以及应用它时需要考虑的关键权衡。
你可能会注意到某些 kernel 出现得非常频繁！特别是对于 Qwen，批量矩阵乘法 kernel 在一个步骤中运行超过 30,000 次。
在本例中，我们将首先探讨融合 kernel。融合 kernel 将多个较小的 GPU kernel 组合成一个单元。这可以通过避免 GPU 的高带宽内存与其更高带宽的片上内存之间代价高昂的传输来帮助提升性能。此外，它还可以实现更高效的 GPU 核心调度。
有了这么多额外的 kernel，虽然 torch.compile 可能可行，但运行起来会花费很长时间。因此，使用手动融合的 kernel 来减少原始算子数量是很好的第一步。此外，像 Flash Attention 这样众所周知的融合并不是 torch.compile 自身能够发现的。
transformers 库默认对标准注意力层使用 torch 的 SDPA 。但事实证明，我们看到的许多小运算来自非标准的门控 delta 网络层。幸运的是，对于这些层，有两个 kernel——causal-conv1d 和 flash-linear-attention——它们被编写用于融合每层中的许多此类运算。我们如何发现这一点？Qwen 的 transformers 库实现 已经告诉我们它支持哪些 kernel：
我们通常推荐第一种，尤其是配合我们的 docker 容器支持 ，在构建时将所有 kernel 安装到容器中，以减少作业启动所需的时间。
虽然 kernelhub 很方便，但由于 kernel 通常明确依赖于所安装的 torch 和 cuda 版本，你的特定配置可能没有可用的 kernel，而 transformers 模型会静默回退到未优化、性能低下的 kernel。
在安装了 flash-linear-attention 和 causal-conv1d 这两个 Python 包之后，我们将端到端时间提升了 3.7 倍，降至 2 小时 5 分钟。在下表中，你可以看到新的内核（已高亮显示）取代了之前表中的逐元素函数。同时，执行的操作总数也大幅减少了 15 倍：

items.excerpt:
The 2026 warehouse management systems market is more useful as a map of architectural and operating differences than as a league table. Providers can share a WMS label while differing materially in execution depth, extensibility, automation orchestration, decision support, deployment model, and the operating environments they are designed to serve.
For warehouse management systems, useful dimensions include operational depth, breadth of supported workflows, architecture and interoperability, intelligence, execution connectivity, and proven outcomes. The relevant metrics include inventory accuracy, order cycle time, throughput, labor productivity, dock-to-stock time, order accuracy, exception volume, automation utilization, and recovery time after disruption. Together these dimensions show where a provider creates value and where additional systems or operating capabilities are still required. The Market Map should therefore be read through the systems principle in Select Technology for the System, Not the Feature List : provider position is useful only when it is translated into fit with the buyer’s actual operating architecture.
The 2026 market can be understood through several broad archetypes: enterprise warehouse specialists; broad supply-chain suite providers; cloud-native and midmarket WMS platforms; and execution/automation-centric platforms that increasingly overlap with WES and orchestration. Each archetype carries different strengths, implementation assumptions, ecosystem dependencies, and likely buyer fit.
A provider that is exceptionally strong in one part of the market may be a poor choice for an organization whose critical requirements sit elsewhere. Market position should therefore be read as analytical context rather than a substitute for requirements-based selection.
The surrounding architecture is ERP and OMS upstream; WMS at the inventory-and-work core; WES/WCS, robotics, conveyors, sortation, labor systems, YMS, parcel, and TMS around the execution edge. An ETH Zurich scientist has shown that bacteria and digital manufacturing can also be used to build free-form architectural elements.
The process is seen as a promising, less energy-intensive alternative to cement. Previously, it has primarily been used to stabilise soils, moulded tiles, and in research.
The research suggests that living bacteria can bond sand and other loose grains together into a solid material by forming calcium carbonate, the mineral that makes up limestone.
The process looks in part like 3D printing (see video below).
Cement manufacturing is one of the largest sources of CO2 emissions in the construction industry. At the Department of Architecture, Karen Antorveza Paez , who has just completed her doctorate at ETH Zurich, is researching an alternative that works in a totally different way: instead of firing rocks at over 1,000°C, she is getting bacteria to bond grains of sand together into solid architectural elements.
“We’re using bacteria to produce a sort of mineral glue,” explains Antorveza Paez.
When certain types of bacteria are combined with sand or other solid grains, they join the particles together into a solid structure made of interlocking, microscopic calcite crystals.
The process is called microbiologically induced calcite precipitation (MICP), or simply biocementation. It’s nothing new: the bacteria used for this, Sporosarcina pasteurii, have been under research for many years, such as for stabilising loose subsoil.
They have also been used in concrete research for “self-healing” concrete, where the introduction of bacterial spores causes cracks to seal over on their own.
Antorveza Paez’s innovation is how the process is controlled: not as an addition to existing building materials, but as an architectural material in its own right. To achieve this, she combined two research fields that had until then been largely separate: biocementation and digital manufacturing.
While it has long been known that bacteria can bond sand together into solid objects under certain conditions, Antorveza Paez explains that, “What was missing were manufacturing processes whereby these biological processes can be controlled as required and used to make architectural elements”.
In the course of writing her doctoral thesis, three scientific studies were conducted that describe two different manufacturing methods.

Neura Robotics has launched Neuron AI, its multimodal foundation model for physical AI.
Combining 3D vision, touch, audio, robot state and language with memory, Neuron AI enables robots to act on information beyond what cameras alone can capture, as well as retain relevant context when objects disappear from view.
Its “Perception-Language-Action” (PLA) architecture connects what a robot sees, hears and feels with what it has already done, turning multisensory information into physical action.
David Reger, founder and CEO of Neura Robotics, says: “An intelligent robot needs a brain that brings its senses together and remembers what happened.
“With Neuron AI, we are building the brain of the physical world: Physical AI that turns human expertise and physical experience into capabilities robots can learn and apply. Developed in Germany, built for the world.”
Cameras capture geometry, color and position, but provide no information about contact, force or sound. Humans also rely on more than sight: they feel whether a screw has caught and hear when a connector clicks into place.
Neuron AI applies this principle to robots. Rather than treating each sensor as a separate input, the model encodes 3D vision, tactile and force data, audio, robot state and language, aligns them in one shared space over time, and turns them into a single stream of action.
Multisensory perception matters most for tasks that cameras cannot solve on their own. When a robot opens a lock, only sound and touch confirm that it is really open. With touch, a robot can grasp objects it cannot see.
The additional senses also improve tasks that vision can already handle: in welding, for example, the quality of a seam can be judged from the sound of the process.
In addition, Neuron AI has a memory function. To act in the physical world, a robot needs a sense of cause and effect and object permanence, the ability to remember objects when they are out of sight, which humans acquire in their first two years of life.
Unlike purely digital AI, a robot acts in a continuous physical world and must keep track of objects and the consequences of its own actions over time, often without seeing them.
Neura adapted the model’s architecture specifically to introduce memory and trains it on dedicated datasets that make use of it.

items.excerpt:
Maintaining software with the GPT-6 family
OpenAI Core Experimentation 团队发文介绍用 GPT-6 Astra 和 GPT-6.1 Sol 配合 Codex 做代码维护，包括清理无用代码和陈旧实验、修复 flaky 测试等。
OpenAI 团队亲述用 GPT-6 系列在 Codex 里清理死代码和陈旧实验，附带 Prompt 思路和成本对比数据，方法可直接迁移到自己的代码库。
每个不断增长的代码库都需要维护：移除无用代码、清理已完成的实验、修复测试。在 OpenAI，编码智能体帮助我们更快地构建，这也增加了我们的维护需求。
我在 OpenAI 的核心实验团队工作，我们负责构建和维护支持公司各项实验的软件，从前端更新到模型服务效率的改进。
GPT-6 Astra 的发布帮助我们更快地构建和维护软件，而 GPT-6.1 Sol 以更低的成本交付了类似的结果。在这篇文章中，我将分享我们如何使用这些模型来发现清理机会、收集证据，并准备变更以供审查。
在智能体编码出现之前，许多软件工程团队依赖与运行时日志集成的复杂静态分析系统来检测和移除无用代码。即使有这些系统和细致的代码审查，错误仍会发生。我记得有几次因误删代码而导致的事故。需要考虑的边缘情况太多了，比如反射会干扰静态分析，或者某条未使用的代码路径可能被激活以缓解未来的事故。
借助 Codex 中的 GPT-5.6 Sol，我可以指定一个要调查的区域和明确的验证标准，然后让模型编写静态分析并移除死代码。这些有针对性的提示比我们现有的静态分析系统更容易开发和维护，可靠性也相当。
当我们获得 GPT-6 Astra 的访问权限后，我们想看看它能否处理更宽泛的请求，自行判断该从哪里入手、需要哪些证据来为每一次删除提供依据。我们从一个简短的 Codex 提示开始，这个提示对 GPT-5.6 Sol 来说过于模糊，无法完全处理。就是下面这个，连拼写错误都保留着：
Astra 很好地处理了这种模糊性。它查看了过去的 PR，从 Slack 讨论串中收集上下文，并检查了内部项目跟踪器。它阅读了生产性能分析表，以确认被删除的代码行从未被执行到。Astra 还解释了每次删除的理由，这加快了我们的审查速度。
看到 Astra 表现如此出色后，五名工程师协作在各个代码库中运行该提示的变体，我们合并了 1400 多个拉取请求，删除了超过 80 万行代码。我们主要是在从事其他项目的同时，利用两周的业余时间完成了这部分工作的大部分。代码审查被分派给各个团队，并附上每个受影响项目的相关背景。这些删除带来了可衡量的收益。例如，某个服务的容器镜像从 3.31GB 缩小到 1.72GB，减少了 48%；另一组清理则从我们的测试套件中移除了约 400 个视觉快照变体。
软件维护中一个更难的问题是清理 过时 的实验。这些实验未必是无用的：它们的代码可能仍在生产环境中运行，或者依赖于随时可能变化的资格评估，这使得静态分析困难得多。过去，我们团队通过确定性的静态分析并辅以数据库查询来清理过时实验，并使用我们最强大的模型（当时是 GPT-5.6 Sol）来构建和改进相关脚本。我们知道这导致了许多假阴性，即我们的分析无法识别出真正过时的实验。

items.title: Google DeepMind and Singapore Government collaborate to build fine-tuned AI model for scam detection
items.description: Learn how Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore uses lightweight on-device Gemma models to intercept conversational scams in private chats with zero cloud data egress.
items.excerpt:
Collaborating with the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech Singapore) to protect users without compromising privacy.
Scams, such as investment fraud, fake job offers, and impersonation of public officials make up over half of Singapore’s reported crimes, and account for more than S$4 billion in losses since 2019 . At the same time, scam tactics have shifted from simple phishing to complex social engineering, whereby attackers manipulate victims with convincing conversations before requesting money. Such scams now account for up to 80% of all losses.
To address this, Google DeepMind and the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech Singapore) have been working together as part of our National AI Partnership with the Singapore Government. Together, we've fine-tuned a privacy-preserving, on-device scam detection model.
Generic models often struggle with local deception techniques, making scam detection harder. To address this, Google’s lightweight Gemma model was fine-tuned on local scam conversations. These ranged from impersonations of public institutions, banks, and local figures, to trending regional schemes. This ensures the fine-tuned model will be able to distinguish benign social chatter from genuine manipulation when deployed in applications installed by citizens.
Unlike traditional threat detection, which relies on server-side scanning of messages in the cloud, this model can process conversation data directly on-device. When integrated into applications, this will allow faster analysis of conversation patterns to detect manipulative intent and help citizens act before financial or credential exposure can occur.
The roll out of the model within applications will be carefully phased and developed in partnership with the Singapore Government. When deployed, the model will only be able to access on-device conversations with the user's consent, in accordance with the terms of use of that application. As the model runs entirely on-device, neither the Singapore Government nor Google, will be able to access users’ conversations through its deployment.
Fighting scams shouldn't mean sacrificing personal privacy. Working with Google DeepMind, we're bringing advanced AI protection directly onto citizens' devices. This allows us to catch highly targeted, local scam attempts in real time while keeping personal communications private.

items.description: Modal 宣布年化收入突破 10 亿美元，并完成 7.5 亿美元 D 轮融资，投后估值 157.5 亿美元，由 Accel 领投，Kleiner Perkins 及现有投资方跟投。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/x5umoaa0xhd8n76uysjppz2fa
items.excerpt:
Modal crosses $1B in Annualized Run Rate and raises $750M Series D
Modal 宣布年化收入突破 10 亿美元，并完成 7.5 亿美元 D 轮融资，投后估值 157.5 亿美元，由 Accel 领投，Kleiner Perkins 及现有投资方跟投。
作者作为当事方给出融资规模、估值和业务数据，并说明自研底层技术栈与新产品线，读者可据此了解 Modal 的增长轨迹。
就在五个月前，当我们宣布 C 轮融资时，我写道 需求正在加速 。自那以后，使用量增长了两倍，我们的同比增速超过 15 倍。我们最近突破了 10 亿美元的年化运行率，且丝毫没有放缓的迹象。
很明显，AI 开启了一整套全新的软件能力。如今存在着许多以前根本无法构建的惊人应用。旧的技术栈并不太适合它们。它们需要不同的构建模块，以及一种全新的基础设施思维方式。
我们正在为大量这类应用提供支持。其中包括 TypeSafe AI 的 Jev，它是有史以来增长最快的产品之一。它在头三天里就在 Modal 上处理了 1T tokens ，而 TypeSafe 团队则专注于交付，而不是管理基础设施。
DoorDash 的 AI 平台团队使用 Modal 将公司各处的应用从实验推进到生产。Cognition、Ramp、Linear 和 Hebbia 正在构建各自领域内的后台智能体专家。Runway 正在世界各个地区生成逼真的视频。Physical Intelligence、Generalist AI 和 1X 正在训练机器人。Chai Discovery 和 Achira 在 Modal 上运行药物发现，通过 Claude Science 开展工作的科学家们也是如此。
软件的每一次转变都会改变人们能构建什么，以及构建它所需的基础设施。我从九十年代初就开始写软件，这并不是第一次阶跃式变化：我们经历过 Web、云、大数据、移动，以及其他几次转变。
当云刚起步时，你突然不得不应对分布式系统、分片和配置管理。我们原有的工具都不是为此而构建的，所以开发者创造了新的工具：Docker、Kubernetes、Terraform 等等。
AI 带来的摩擦如今已经相当明显。GPU 稀缺，模型相当大且加载缓慢。LLM 现在会写代码了！而且它必须在某个地方运行，与其他一切隔离开来。当然，你可以在旧技术栈上为所有这些考量进行构建，很多人也确实这么做了，但最终你会陷入 YAML 地狱和 GPU 采购炼狱。
所以我们深入了下去。我们抛弃了大部分现有技术栈，在一个如今横跨 20 多个云的容量池上，从零开始构建了自己的文件系统、容器运行时、调度器和网络。
软件之美在于可组合性。如果你拥有合适的构建模块——通用、久经考验且可扩展——你就能构建出无限组合的东西。
函数是我们的第一个构建模块：你编写代码，Modal 来运行它。事实证明这非常有用，尤其是对生成式 AI：用扩散模型生成图像、Suno 的音乐、用 vLLM 和 SGLang 进行 LLM 推理，以及模型训练。
我们在 2023 年推出了 Sandboxes，当时我们注意到人们正在使用 LLM 生成代码。Sandboxes 爆发式增长，三年后，它仅凭自身就成为一个年运行率 3 亿美元的产品。用例范围从后台智能体，到强化学习、vibecoding 平台，等等。我们已经启动了近 30 亿个 sandbox，它们可以扩展到 百万级并发 。
我们最近推出了 多节点训练 —— 一个装饰器就能为你提供一个完全 RDMA 连接的集群，无需容量承诺。我们正在向上层推进，并推出了一系列 RL 和后训练方面的产品。
在推理方面，我们一直在推出 Modal 服务器 ，这是更适合 HTTP 服务器的解决方案，以及一些围绕 LLM 服务的非常酷的功能，例如 端点候选 。
五年前我们创立 Modal 时，我无法想象今天在上面运行的绝大多数应用。同样难以想象两年后人们将创造的软件，但我确信的是，它将需要一套全新的构建模块。我们希望其中很多都能在 Modal 上运行。
为了继续构建未来，我们完成了 7.5 亿美元的 D 轮融资，投后估值 157.5 亿美元。本轮由 Accel 领投。Kleiner Perkins 加入，我们所有现有投资者均参与其中，包括 Menlo Ventures、General Catalyst、Redpoint、Lux Capital 和 Bain Capital Ventures。

Oct 14, 2026 Introducing Grok Voice 3.0 The world’s most intelligent voice model. Read More
xAI 发布 speech-to-speech 模型 Grok Voice 3.0，在 Artificial Analysis 的 Speech-to-Speech Index 以 86.9 分排名第一，时延低于一秒。
官方发布给出多项第三方基准分数、时延和 API 定价，读者可以据此评估它在语音智能体场景的性价比。
今天，我们宣布推出 Grok Voice 3.0，全球最智能的语音到语音模型。它在解决客户支持通话方面创下新纪录，延迟处于同类领先水平，低于一秒，且成本低于其他前沿模型。Grok Voice 每天为 Tesla 和 SpaceX 的数百万次对话提供支持，今天已在 API 中上线，价格与前代相同。
在 Artificial Analysis 的独立测试中，Grok Voice 3.0 在 Speech-to-Speech Index 上排名第一，得分为 86.9。该指数综合了语音推理、 τ -Voice，以及盲测一对一通话中的偏好和任务成功率。Grok Voice 3.0 在 Full Duplex Bench 上也获得 97% 的分数，该基准衡量其处理停顿、轮流发言和打断的自然程度。
τ -Voice 衡量智能体处理带有不同口音、背景噪音和打断的支持通话的能力。Grok Voice 3.0 得分为 71.6%，与 GPT-Live-1（Astra）相当，但延迟低 40%，在智能体智能与响应速度之间树立了新的前沿。
它的运行成本也低于同类模型。Artificial Analysis 测量了每个模型在其 Big Bench Audio 运行中完成任务所需的成本，Grok Voice 3.0 低于 GPT-Live-1（Astra，Medium）和 GPT-Realtime-2.1。
Artificial Analysis 的 Big Bench Audio 运行中每任务平均成本，美元。越低越好。
在 EVA-Bench 上，即 ServiceNow 面向企业语音智能体的基准，Grok Voice 3.0 取得了 74% 的最高准确率得分，并且在准确率和客户体验的综合评分中表现最佳。
Grok Voice 3.0 每天在 Tesla 车辆中处理数百万次对话。驾驶员可以使用 Connectors 处理简单请求，例如查看日历或回复电子邮件，并使用 Grok Bot 处理更大的任务，例如点咖啡或预订晚餐——全程完全免手操作（ 在 X 上查看 ）。Grok Voice 3.0 也为 Grok Bot 的语音模式提供支持。
Starlink 呼叫中心使用 Grok Voice 每天以多种语言接听 20,000 通客户来电。约 70% 无需人工介入即可解决，四分之一的销售通话在来电者挂断前完成购买。一个基于 Grok Voice 3.0 构建的单一代理即可验证客户身份、排查硬件故障、发放信用额度并寄送替换设备。
Grok Voice 3.0 即日起在 Voice Agent API 中提供，价格为 $0.08 / 分钟（$4.80 / 小时） ，与 Grok Voice 2.0 相同。使用 grok-voice-latest 的代理已自动切换，无需任何更改。

Adaptive Verification Without a Confidence Head
vLLM 支持 confidence scoring 扩展到所有基于草稿模型的投机类型，通过在线拟合的 logistic 回归从草发者 logits 推导 logit(q_max) 特征来预测目标模型的接受概率，作为 Adaptive Verification 的置信分。
原文给出无置信头草稿模型启用 Adaptive Verification 的在线估计方法、设计取舍和实测数据，方法可直接在 vLLM 中配置复用。
现在所有基于草稿模型的推测器类型都支持置信度评分。在没有置信度头的情况下， 在线拟合估计器 从草稿模型的 logits 中提取特征，以预测目标模型接受它的概率，该概率直接用作自适应验证的置信度分数。估计器的系数会持续拟合，以适应传入的数据流量。该功能已在 PR #52228 中落地，对于没有置信度头的草稿模型，可通过 enable_adaptive_verification 启用。
vLLM 的 自适应验证 （AV）能够在推测解码期间验证一部分草稿 token。接受概率较低的草稿 token 会在运行目标模型前向传播之前从批次中裁剪掉，从而节省计算量。这种优化在服务大批量时尤其有益，因为在这种情况下 GPU 会变得受计算限制。更多细节请参见 这篇 vLLM 博客文章 。
AV 需要每个 token 的接受概率估计，这就是为什么到目前为止它只支持 DSpark 草稿模型。DSpark 模型通常附带一个置信度头：在每个位置上对草稿模型隐藏状态应用一个小型线性层，训练为二元分类器，判断“目标模型会接受这个 token 吗？”
缺少置信度头的草稿模型，例如 EAGLE、MTP、DFlash 以及一些 DSpark 检查点，完全无法使用 AV。要使用它，这些草稿模型需要每个 token 的接受度估计，而添加置信度头意味着重新训练草稿模型，对于人们已经在服务的许多现有检查点来说，这不是一个可行的选项。
使用草稿模型自身的置信度作为接受度的代理已被广泛确立。 EAGLE-2 表明 EAGLE 的草稿概率与接受率紧密相关，并用它们来扩展和重排动态草稿树。 Draft & Verify 及若干后续工作一旦草稿模型的概率低于固定阈值就停止草稿。 SpecDec++ 则训练一个专门的接受预测头，在思路上与 DSpark 的置信度头类似。在每种情况下，从草稿置信度到接受度的映射要么按原样使用，要么离线学习。
AV 需要的不仅仅是一个好的排序。它的预算决策会对预测的接受概率求和，并将其与实测成本进行权衡，因此预测必须针对所服务的特定模型对和工作负载进行校准，这正是下一节中在线拟合估计器所提供的内容。
我们添加了一个轻量级逻辑回归，从草稿分布导出的单个标量——草稿模型最可能 token 的对数几率——来估计每个草稿 token 的接受概率。每个草稿位置有一个共享斜率和截距，因此一个 K token 的草稿模型总共需要 K + 1 个参数。这些参数从目标模型在正常验证期间已经产生的接受/拒绝决策中在线拟合。任何现有的草稿检查点都能免费获得 AV。
本节剩余部分涵盖该设计的两个部分：估计器对什么量进行评分，以及其系数在服务期间如何拟合。
其中 ω 是在所有草稿位置上共享的拟合斜率，β i 是拟合的逐位置截距， q 是草稿分布。另一种对数几率形式使这一关系更加清晰：
logit( q max ) 是该估计器的特征，即草稿最可能 token 的对数几率。直观地说，它表示草稿模型对其预测的置信程度。它被系数 ω 和 β i 线性变换，以预测草稿被目标模型接受的对数几率。其 sigmoid 值即为 p ，即估计的接受率，用作 AV 的置信度分数。

无损性是这些特征必须具备的不可协商属性。否则，我们就破坏了投机解码输出目标模型精确分布这一根本保证。AUC 和 ECE 对 AV 的裁剪决策都很重要，但方式不同。AUC 对生存概率的 局部排序 很重要：
AUC 确保更可能被接受的草稿 token 优先于不太可能被接受的 token 被接纳。另一方面，ECE 对 全局 预算决策很重要：
这些概率被求和，然后除以实测成本表。ECE 确保估计的被接受 token 数量与现实相符。
下表列出了各种实验过的特征及其在四个类别上的得分。这些得分是在服务 DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark（temp=1，top-p=0.95，conc=64）、未启用 AV 的过程中收集的约 450 万个带标签草稿上测得的，涵盖五个数据集：SPEED-Bench 2k 低/高熵、GSM8K、HumanEval 和 MT-Bench。最后两行是参考项而非拟合特征：直接使用草稿器的 q max 作为接受概率而不进行拟合，以及训练好的置信度头的得分。
logit( q sampled ) 和 −log(−log( q sampled )) 在 AUC 方面明显优于表中选用的特征，但未被采用，因为基于它们进行裁剪会导致输出分布有偏。两者都读取 q sampled ，即 drafter 实际抽取的 token 的概率。基于该值的函数对草稿进行裁剪，会使在位置 i 是否验证的决策依赖于 x i 本身，因此经过裁剪后存活的草稿不再服从 q 分布。标准拒绝采样以概率 min(1, p / q ) 接受一个 token，期望 q 是草稿 token 被采样时所服从的分布。但基于 q sampled 进行裁剪会使输出的分布偏向 drafter 置信度更高的 token。 1
q max 的“不拟合”行说明了我们为何要进行拟合，而不是像 EAGLE-2 在构建草稿树时那样直接使用 drafter 自身的概率。直接使用时，drafter 的 top-token 概率对草稿的排序实际上优于训练后的

items.description: Google 公开发布智能体审阅系统 Deep Review，可对复杂技术文档提供反馈与验证，最初面向计算机科学论文，现已扩展到法律、金融等领域。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/enqtz3wtz6khvf0m44z5a5jaz
items.excerpt:
Analyzing technical documents with Deep Review
Google 公开发布智能体审阅系统 Deep Review，可对复杂技术文档提供反馈与验证，最初面向计算机科学论文，现已扩展到法律、金融等领域。
原文介绍了系统由来、四阶段智能体审阅流程和公开使用条件，读者可以了解其适用范围与接入方式。
生成式 AI 加速了许多技术领域的发展。如今，AI 在撰写科学论文和技术文档、运行代码、设计实验以及起草提案中发挥某种作用已很常见。然而，加速内容创作也带来了评审挑战：在 AI 生成内容快速增加的同时，人类的验证能力基本保持不变。评审长篇科学手稿或复杂法律协议等复杂文档，需要专业知识和深入的学科理解。这种失衡造成了 验证瓶颈 ，即信息生成的速度快于其被严格评审的速度。
今天，我们很高兴地宣布公开发布 Deep Review ，这是一个智能体 AI 系统，旨在为复杂文档提供严格的反馈和技术验证。该系统最初为计算机科学学术论文分析而设计，其能力现已扩展到评审法律、金融等多个领域的文档。它既可作为起草过程中的迭代改进工具，也可作为评审过程中用于科学流程验证、主张核查和评估的工具。
Deep Review 代表了我们 Paper Assistant Tool (PAT) 的演进——这是一项实验性计划，旨在帮助研究人员在会议投稿前对手稿进行压力测试。在过去一年中，我们与四个旗舰计算机科学会议（ STOC 2026 、 ICML 2026、 NeurIPS 2026、 和 ICLR 2027 ）合作，为超过 16,000 篇选择加入的手稿作者提供私密的投稿前反馈。有关 PAT 及这些试点项目的更多细节，可在我们的手稿 Towards Automating Scientific Review with Google’s Paper Assistant Tool 中找到。
验证瓶颈最显著的例子之一是学术同行评审。这体现在学术出版场所——尤其是 AI 研究本身的场所——投稿量的上升，且增幅巨大。今年，三大 AI 会议（ ICLR 、 NeurIPS 和 ICML ）的投稿量超过 74,000 篇， 高于大约 2025 年的 45,000 篇、2024 年的 32,000 篇和 2023 年的 23,000 篇。每一篇投稿都需要多份高质量评审，以确保同行评审流程的完整性，这可能会给人类专家带来更大的负担。
Deep Review 旨在帮助减轻技术领域人类审稿人日益加重的负担。通过对文档提供详细、客观的评估，Deep Review 检查逻辑一致性和数学陈述，提出改进建议，为事实提供依据，并与现有工作进行对比。它处理了审稿中一些认知负担最重的方面，同时将更高层次的判断留给人类。
Deep Review 已在其实验名称 Paper Assistant Tool （PAT）下进行了广泛测试和部署，与旗舰计算机科学会议 STOC 2026、ICML 2026、NeurIPS 2026 和 ICLR 2027 建立了四个试点合作。在这些试点期间，作者可以选择在提交截止日期前几周通过 PAT 接收对其论文的反馈和分析。目标是向作者提供可操作的反馈，以帮助提高提交论文的质量。这些反馈与官方会议审稿流程完全脱钩。PAT 未收集任何数据用于训练，且在每个项目结束后，论文会立即从 Google 系统中删除。
作者对该工具的反应极为积极，也反映出底层模型和 PAT 框架的持续改进。随着 Deep Review 中加入 Gemini 4 Argon 支持，该工具的底层能力已进一步超越下文所述的旧版 PAT。
单提示 LLM 调用在评估长篇、复杂文档时常常失败，原因在于耗尽 token 推理预算、忽略长上下文中的跨章节依赖，或未经充分审视就接受细微的论断。Deep Review 通过一个四阶段智能体流水线解决这些挑战：
虽然 Deep Review 起源于学术论文评审，但长上下文评审具有普适性：用于检查研究论文中数学证明是否成立的推理机制，同样有助于发现其他类型文档中的逻辑漏洞和不一致之处——在这些文档中，论断必须有证据支撑。因此，Deep Review 可用于为更广泛的日常流程带来结构化的批判性评审。

我们还推出了 Teamwork Deep Document Review Pattern ， 这是一种受 Deep Review 启发的文档评审实现模式，已内置于 Antigravity 中，使用 Teamwork 多智能体编排框架 。该模式旨在系统性地评估研究论文、手稿草稿和技术提案，采用具有自我纠正和基于分段的评分标准的多智能体层级结构。Antigravity 用户可以使用 /teamwork-preview 命令调用此模式。
在计算机科学领域，全面的投稿前评审通常依赖于广泛的评审网络——如资深教师、资源充足的学术实验室或广泛的同行咨询网络。提供可靠的自动化逻辑验证，可以帮助许多学者对自己的论断进行压力测试，发现可避免的缺陷，基于经过验证的基础来完善和强化文档，并更有信心地将成果提交到评审流程中。
鉴于它在与学术会议开展的试点项目中展现出的实用性，我们相信像 Deep Review 这样的工具将在未来几年内，通过赋能作者和评审者，在同行评审流程中发挥重要作用。
展望未来，我们将继续扩展该平台的能力。随着 Gemini 4 Argon 支持的推出，Deep Review 的底层能力进一步提升，为作者提供更高质量的反馈和分析。此外，随着多文件支持即将推出，用户还将能够同时对整套相关文档、电子表格和附件运行这些一致性检查。我们希望这些进步能让各地知识工作者更广泛地获得高质量的技术评审。
Deep Review 是 Google Research、Google DeepMind 和 Google Cloud 的协作成果。我们感谢核心贡献者和研究

Redesigning source control at Anthropic ( via ) Interesting piece from Anthropic describing why and how they built their own custom alternative to Git, based on the dramatic increase in rate of changes to their code after the past six months.
In May 2026, Anthropic averaged around 2,500 code changes merged per day; as of September, we merged over 30,000 per day.
They included a chart showing those changes. I had Claude modify their chart ( code here ) to add markers for the public releases of each of their models in 2026:
This shows public release dates, not the date when models became available for Anthropic's internal use. My guess is that the introduction of Fable/Mythos class models is a key factor in the increased coding velocity.
"Antique" is their new code review system. The source control system is called Scion, and sounds to me like a reinvention of centralized source control along the lines of Subversion.
( Update : Anthropic credit Google's Piper and Meta's Sapling as "prior art" - it looks like the core concept of "derived data" was heavily inspired by Mononoke , the server component of Sapling.)
They had some pretty extreme requirements:
The history of our main branch alone is almost 100 GB, and a compressed working copy is over 25 GB. We perform on the order of 25 million code checkouts per day for CI, before counting developer environments, agent sandboxes, and research jobs. Fetched naively, that would be over 600 PB of git traffic per day.
The new system was built by a team of seven people, and the migration from Git was completed in five months.
When asked on Hacker News about the lack of offline support, Scion engineer Nick G replied :
Since Claude is by far the heaviest user of Scion and is necessarily online, this just wasn't important to do.
As an aside, I've been trying adversarial review in my own projects recently, where you have a model try and find flaws (I often play Claude and GPT off against each other). This note from the article reflected my own experience with that:
Anthropic also makes extensive use of adversarial review, and, while this is incredibly effective in many ways, it can also be myopic, so skilled engineers needed to steer Claude away from over-engineering parts of the system in response to hypothetical concerns.

items.excerpt:
I added support to llm-gemini for the new Gemini 4 Argon model, made available today via the Gemini API and for customers of their $100/month subscription plan.
Here are the low, medium and high pelicans . As expected, they are all excellent: Gemini has a track record of producing great SVGs, and are the only lab where I know their staff have invested in SVG specifically (and who have boasted about their pelicans before.)
Here's the "high" illustration, which cost me 17.166 cents:
The pricing is interesting. At launch, Argon is $2/million input and $10/million output - the same price as GPT-6 Sol, half the price of Claude Opus 5.5 and 1/5th the price of Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.
But on December 1st Argon is set to double in price - so it will be the same price as Opus 5.5.
Prices like this aren't really comparable these days since what really matters is how many tokens a model takes to achieve a goal within an agentic harness.
One useful clue for that comes from Artificial Analysis, who publish the total cost to run their benchmark using each model. Argon is looking very good there - costing $2,407 to run the benchmark, putting it close to GLM-5.3 and significantly cheaper than OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta's latest models.
When the price doubles it will still be a little cheaper than GPT-6 Astra.
(I used ChatGPT to edit that chart ! The data is all correct, I checked - I needed to get that Gemini 4 Argon info box to display without overlapping the other numbers.)
Some bonus examples using Gemini 4 Argon: here's Generate an SVG of an armadillo in fishnet tights jaywalking on Mars , here's a Fabergé egg it created for me using Blender, and DeepMind staffer @fofrAI shared a video of a pelican riding a bike, using fourier epicycles . That's a fun new twist!

items.excerpt:
Watch along AIE NYC and join us at AIE CODE in SF next month!
This episode includes a live demo of the Taku robot that is best enjoyed on YouTube .
Last month, Dyna made waves by announcing Dyna-2 , a world-action model pre-trained on one million hours of human video, claiming several new scaling laws on human data across four orders of magnitude . They have now followed up the model with a physical robot agent, Dyna-2.1 , that has to be seen to be believed:
In his talk at AIE this year, Jason talked about how the real challenge for robotics in the real world is reliable, long-horizon autonomy , and how Dyna got its models to a 99.4% success rate folding restaurant napkins for 24 hours straight, including recovering after it pulled over the whole stack.
From training a world-action model on over one million hours of human video to deploying robots that fold thousands of napkins daily at Din Tai Fung , Dyna Robotics is pushing physical AI beyond impressive demos and into real-world production. In this episode, Dyna Robotics co-founder and Chief Scientist Jason Ma joins swyx on-site to unpack how robots can learn new tasks from as little as 45 minutes of demonstrations, why predicting the future of the physical world may be the key to general-purpose robotics, and what it actually takes to build robots that work reliably for real customers.
We go deep on Dyna-2, Dyna’s million-hour world-action model that combines future video prediction with robot actions, the scaling laws behind human-to-robot transfer, diffusion transformers and flow matching, and why synthetic environments and self-generated training data could unlock the next wave of robotics progress. Jason also explains why Dyna builds its own hardware instead of relying on off-the-shelf humanoids, how agentic harnesses enable robots to execute hour-long workflows, why dexterous hands and missing sensory data remain major bottlenecks, and what separates real commercial deployments from the graveyard of robotics startups. We also cover world-action models versus vision-language-action models, GPT-6 and coding agents in robotics, and Jason’s journey from AlphaGo and Penn to NVIDIA, Google DeepMind, and founding Dyna.

Visual Studio Copilot and SSMS Remote Code Execution (CVE-2026-103572)
Johann Rehberger 披露 Visual Studio Copilot 与 SQL Server Management Studio 中的远程代码执行漏洞 CVE-2026-103572，根因是利用文件名末尾多加一个点绕过路径校验，写入 .mcp. 或 settings.VisualStudio. 等受保护配置文件，实现任意命令执行。
作者亲述漏洞原理与利用链，读者可学到 Windows 路径规范化缺陷如何绕过 AI 智能体安全检查的可迁移方法。
今天微软 发布了补丁 ，修复了我八月份报告的 Visual Studio Copilot 中的一个漏洞。微软将其归类为 Important 严重级别的 Remote Code Execution 漏洞。
其根本原因是，它允许 Visual Studio 或 SQL Server Management Studio 中的 Copilot 绕过路径验证检查，写入自己的设置和配置文件 。这使得 Copilot 能够突破隔离限制，实现任意命令执行。
在我提交给 MSRC 的报告中，我还演示了第三方如何通过间接提示注入来利用它实现远程命令执行。
它同时影响 Visual Studio 和 SQL Server Management Studio。核心漏洞位于一个共享的易受攻击的 Copilot DLL 中，名为 Microsoft.VisualStudio.Copilot.Core.dll 。包括 Visual Studio 2022 在内的旧版本也受到影响。
元老级 Visual Studio 产品是广泛使用的企业开发环境。它还集成了 GitHub Copilot，目前以 Visual Studio 2026 的形式发布。
很多人不知道的是，SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) 基于相同的代码和外壳，因此一个 IDE 中的许多漏洞也适用于另一个。
你看，在 Windows 中，文件名末尾可以有 . ，这完全有效且会被 忽略 。底层的 NTFS 系统会区分名称差异，但 Win32 层只是忽略末尾的点。
以 ASCII 句点 (0x2E) 字符结尾的文件和文件夹名称在保存时也会去掉该字符。
注意：如果对你们有些人有用的话，使用扩展长度路径语法 (\?) 可以访问那些正常 Win32 路径处理会进行规范化的文件名。
现在，这是本应阻止 Copilot 写入 Visual Studio 和 SSMS 中 mcp 和设置配置文件的代码。

验证通过了，因为这两个字符串不同。然而，当应用程序随后使用常规 Windows 文件 API 写入该文件名时，末尾的点被移除，写入目标变成了 .mcp.json ！
这基本上就是 Copilot 这里的核心漏洞。该漏洞位于 Microsoft.VisualStudio.Copilot.Core.dll 中。
末尾的点让 AI 代理绕过了对敏感配置文件的保护，修改了它本应被明确禁止更改的设置。
在为其编写漏洞利用程序时，我发现了其他问题。其中一些很基础，让我不禁怀疑这怎么能通过代码审查。

这是使 Microsoft AI MAI-Code-1-Flash 模型产生偏差的 POC 演示：
当用户随后与该文件交互时，Copilot 就被劫持了。请注意，此内容也可能通过其他方式进入聊天，例如从 MCP 服务器返回的数据。
注意：第二个 MCP 漏洞利用稍微复杂一些，需要收集本地 VS 安装标识符作为路径名的一部分来找到设置文件，但它在 VS 和 SSMS 上也都有效。
我在验证 SQL Copilot 安全问题 的修复时发现了这个漏洞。特别是，我注意到添加了对 MCP 的支持，这让我好奇它是如何实现的，并触发了这项调查和漏洞利用。
尽管 Microsoft 将该问题归类为 Important 严重性 Remote Code Execution （CVSS 评分 8.8）并发布了安全修复，但该安全漏洞仍被认为不在赏金奖励范围内。
我希望微软今后在展示并帮助发现其 Copilot 产品中的新型漏洞时，能更公平地奖励研究人员——这些产品每天有数百万人在使用。我有点担心，如果这种情况很普遍，研究人员可能会不再第一时间直接向微软报告漏洞。对我来说，这已经是两个月内第三个导致补丁发布、却没有获得奖励的漏洞了。
我今天花了一些时间查看修复方案，似乎添加了一个对 GetFullPath 的调用，它会移除点号并规范化文件名。在 Windows 上，这会移除末尾的点号，并解析诸如 .. 这样的相对路径组件。这解决了末尾点号绕过问题，也应该能防止我报告的一些路径遍历变体。
希望这是一篇有启发性的文章，能鼓励大家更多地研究 Windows 文件系统和规范化问题。尤其是在 AI 出现之后，此类漏洞及其变体被发现的速度如此之快，我们很可能会看到许多因此而出错的情况。
在这种情况下，我们可以看到，可能只需要一个 . 就能绕过安全检查，让智能体执行任意命令。

Freight rates are being driven to historic highs by the potent effects of a structurally higher-cost transportation environment, heated up by entrenched high fuel prices, capacity constraints, and peak-related fees, according to a report from AFS Logistics and TD Cowen.
The report projects an expensive Q4, with holiday shippers facing record-high ground and express parcel costs, the highest truckload rates since Q1 2022, and LTL rates eclipsing 80% above the January 2018 baseline for the first time ever.
Those are the results of the “TD Cowen/AFS Freight Index,” a snapshot with predictive pricing for truckload, less-than-truckload (LTL), and parcel transportation markets.
“We expect fuel to drive elevated transportation costs for the foreseeable future. Inventories are low and refineries are at capacity, so even if crude oil prices drop in the coming months, diesel and jet fuel supplies must still catch up before prices recede,” says Andy Dyer, CEO, AFS Logistics. “The other key force shaping freight markets is capacity. The holiday rush always places a seasonal premium on parcel capacity, while the continued ascent of truckload rates is the result of steady demand chasing a shrinking pool of trucks.”
For example, the parcel sector could see conditions for a “perfect storm for a pricey peak season,” the report said. Projections for Q4 solidify 2026 as the most expensive parcel shipping year on record, a testament to years of carrier pricing changes designed to maximize revenue in a broad range of market conditions. The fuel surcharge is a prime example, with carriers frequently reindexing surcharge tables since 2021 to not only capture additional revenue as fuel prices rise but keep fuel surcharges high even as actual fuel prices fall.

U.S. container imports reached their highest September volume on record, reaching 24.8% above the pre-Covid mark of September, 2019, according to the Global Shipping Report from supply chain software vendor Descartes.
By the numbers, September imports to the U.S. totaled 2,546,261 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in September 2026, down 2.2% from August and up 10.3% from September 2025.
The increase came despite stormy conditions in worldwide container flows. Descartes cited an array of changes to trade conditions, including: Middle East maritime incidents and new carrier fuel charges added to routing and cost risk; Section 232 tariff treatment for specified pharmaceuticals took effect for additional companies on September 29; the Panama Canal Authority announced a partial restoration of transit capacity; and some carriers are resuming selected Suez Canal services even as Red Sea security remains uncertain.
Much of the increase was driven by China-origin imports, the numbers showed. U.S. containerized imports from China reached 924,454 TEUs in September 2026, increasing 40,136 TEUs (4.5%) from August and 161,682 TEUs (21.2%) from September 2025 (see Figure 4). China represented 36.3% of total U.S. container imports, up from 34.0% in August.
China’s September import mix was led by plastics (HS-39), at 135,097 TEUs (14.6% of China-origin volume), followed by furniture and bedding (HS-94), at 123,574 TEUs (13.4%), and toys and sporting goods (HS-95), at 92,842 TEUs (about 10%). Machinery (HS-84) and electrical machinery (HS-85) accounted for a combined 17.6%, while apparel, made-up textiles, and footwear (HS-61 through HS-64) represented 11.1%.

items.title: From Prompting to Persistent Decision Workflows in Supply Chain Operations
items.description: From Prompting to Persistent Decision Workflows in Supply Chain Operations describes the move from episodic AI assistance to an operating capability. Repeated prompting can help an analyst investigate a problem, but supply chains do not operate as a series of isolated conversations. The post From Prompting to Persistent Decision Workflows in Supply Chain Operations appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Supply-chain AI is moving from episodic prompting toward persistent decision workflows. Repeated prompting can help an analyst solve a problem, but an operating capability must maintain context, monitor changing state, preserve decision logic, and connect recommendations to the work that follows.
A persistent decision workflow needs memory of the business object, the current plan, previous recommendations, overrides, policies, and outcomes. Without that continuity, users repeatedly reconstruct context and the model cannot reliably distinguish a new exception from a continuation of an old one. This persistence requirement becomes more important as the AI-agent execution model advances, because an agent cannot act safely if each interaction starts without durable operating state or prior decision context.
A mature design connects detection, context assembly, analysis, option generation, recommendation, approval, execution, and feedback. Some stages may use generative AI; others are better handled by optimization, rules, deterministic integrations, or human judgment. Persistence comes from the workflow and state model, not from the conversational interface.
The system should know what it may observe, recommend, prepare, execute, and escalate. Financial thresholds, customer impact, reversibility, confidence, and policy can determine the autonomy level. These controls make repeated decisions governable at scale.
ERP, planning, TMS, WMS, visibility, risk, and network platforms remain systems of record and execution; decision intelligence sits above and across them where context is assembled, tradeoffs are evaluated, actions are prioritized, and responses are coordinated. The persistent workflow therefore needs controlled write-back or action mechanisms, not only read access and summarization.

items.excerpt:
LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a 24B-parameter reasoning model with just 2B active parameters, built for fast, private agents on-device. It thinks before it answers, calls tools, and works through multi-step tasks inside popular agent harnesses. Because only 2B parameters are active per token, each reasoning token is cheap, so you can run agents continuously on your own hardware.
LFM2.5-24B-A2B builds on LFM2-24B-A2B and keeps its architecture: 40 layers, 64 experts per MoE block with top-4 routing, and the same hybrid of gated short convolutions and GQA. The context window grows from 32K to 131K tokens, and an in-place tokenizer expansion doubles the vocabulary from 65K to 128K tokens for better non-Latin tokenization. Unlike its predecessor, it is a reasoning-only model that produces an explicit chain of thought before its final answer.
Pre-training was scaled up from ~17T to ~33T tokens. Mid-training then adds 2T tokens at 32K context, weighted toward reasoning, math, code, instruction following, and multilingual text, and 300B tokens at 131K context, weighted toward long-context data. Tool calls and multi-turn trajectories appear throughout both phases. Post-training turns the base model into an agent in five stages:

It is the smallest model in the group, yet it is competitive with MoEs with ~50% more total and active parameters.

It also leads on all three instruction-following benchmarks. Most people still think Elon Musk’s biggest projects are rockets and robots. According to long-time technology analyst Josh Baylin, they may be looking in the wrong place.
Baylin, the same researcher who briefed Congress in 2004 about the coming smartphone revolution (three years before the iPhone), now argues that Musk is quietly assembling the pieces for something far more disruptive: a true AI phone. He calls it the Starphone.
In his latest presentation, Baylin lays out a clear case. SpaceX has already secured nationwide spectrum, filed trademarks for “Starlink Mobile,” partnered with major chipmakers, received new FCC approvals, and begun launching orbital data-center satellites.
At the same time, Musk controls one of the most capable AI models available today through Grok. Baylin’s central question is simple: why build every critical layer of the technology stack only to let someone else put the final device in people’s pockets?
He believes the logical next step is a thinner, lower-cost device that connects directly to satellites, offloads heavy processing to space-based computers, and continuously improves through software updates. In other words, a phone that does not need traditional cell towers and never becomes obsolete the way today’s handsets do.
What makes the thesis especially interesting for investors is Baylin’s focus. He is not primarily recommending SpaceX or Tesla shares. Instead, he points to the suppliers that will build the essential components inside such a device.
Historically, when major new platforms launch, the companies making the critical parts often deliver some of the largest percentage gains.
Baylin freely names Qualcomm as a starting point because of its existing work with SpaceX on satellite connectivity chips. He says a longer list of additional suppliers appears in a dedicated research report.
That report, along with a full year of ongoing analysis, is currently available through his True Innovations Report service. You can review the complete details and the current offer here: Josh Baylin Starphone .
Baylin’s broader body of work adds context to the claim. In addition to his longer-term technology research, he has also developed a shorter-term system called Mosaic Trader.
That service uses a proprietary Shadow Data Indicator to identify tech stocks showing unusual signals that often appear weeks before major announcements.

Ubitium , a semiconductor startup building a “universal processor” for machines that perceive, think and act in the real world, has announced $14 million in new seed funding.
The round was led by Ibex Investors, with participation from OpenOcean, existing investors including KBC Focus Fund, Runa Capital and Inflection, and Florian Seibel, co-founder and co-CEO of European defence technology company Quantum Systems, investing personally.
It brings Ubitium’s total seed funding to $18 million since the company was founded in 2024.
Ubitium’s thesis is simple: autonomous machines need three kinds of computing to work together so they can perceive, think and act in the real world. The company is building one universal processor to replace the stack of specialised chips often stitched together to do that work today.
The funding follows the return of Ubitium’s first silicon, taped out a year after the company was founded, which demonstrated that signal processing, AI inference and real-time control can all run on one processor architecture.
Physical AI is artificial intelligence built into machines that do physical work, such as drones, robots, vehicles and industrial equipment. General-purpose robotics alone could become a $370 billion market by 2040 under McKinsey’s base-case forecast.

Scan Computers has entered into a partnership with Sheffield-based OLO Robotics , combining Scan’s robotics hardware, AI infrastructure and technical expertise with OLO’s browser-based platform and specialist robotics engineering, to make advanced robotics easier to access and deploy.
OLO’s platform brings teleoperation, simulation and autonomous navigation together in the browser. With it, you can quickly and easily test robots in a safe virtual environment, monitoring their sensors and developing code that determines their behaviour, before deploying them in the real world.
Because it needs no installation, OLO can be used from practically any device, and it runs on top of ROS 2, so each robot keeps its full features and capabilities.
The new partnership allows Scan to make its range of Unitree robots accessible to teams without specialist ROS developers, adding further value to the platforms.
Customers can pair a Unitree robot from Scan with OLO and go from unboxing to autonomous navigation, whether the goal is industrial inspection, academic research or prototyping.
Akash Raja, Director of Robotics at Scan, said: “OLO Robotics’ innovative and user-friendly software perfectly complements our own ecosystem of GPU-accelerated robots, strengthening our position as a complete solution provider for robotics in the UK.”
Eleanor Tang-Smith, co-founder and COO of OLO Robotics, said: “Buying a capable robot has become straightforward. Getting it to do useful work is still the hard part, and it usually depends on specialist ROS engineers who are in short supply.
“Working with Scan means a customer can unbox a robot, connect it through a browser and start building inspection, research or prototyping applications without that barrier. Together we can give organisations a complete route from first idea to deployment.”
Scan is an Nvidia Elite Partner and OLO Robotics is a member of the Nvidia Inception programme . OLO Robotics will be at the Scan stand 3068 at Nvidia GTC Berlin, October 20-22nd.

items.excerpt:
Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems (AS/RS) have become a cornerstone of modern warehouse automation strategies. Whether the technology involves shuttles, cube-based systems, cranes, or goods-to-person solutions, the business case is typically built around a common set of objectives: increasing throughput, reducing labor requirements, improving accuracy, and maximizing storage utilization. Yet one of the most important decisions in any AS/RS implementation often receives far less attention than the technology itself: SKU selection.
Companies frequently spend months evaluating vendors, software platforms, and automation architectures. However, even the most advanced AS/RS can fail to deliver expected returns if the wrong products are placed into the system. In many cases, the difference between a highly successful deployment and a disappointing investment comes down to a simple question: Which SKUs should be automated?
One of the most common misconceptions about AS/RS is that its primary purpose is to store inventory. While increased storage density is certainly a benefit, the real value of automation lies in improving warehouse productivity.
AS/RS creates value by reducing manual labor associated with inventory handling. Every automated retrieval eliminates walking, searching, traveling, and material movement. The more frequently a product is handled, the greater the opportunity for automation to generate measurable savings.
This is where SKU velocity becomes critical.
Not all inventory contributes equally to warehouse activity. In most distribution centers, a relatively small percentage of SKUs generates a disproportionately large percentage of order lines, picks, and replenishment activity. These high-velocity items create the majority of warehouse work and therefore present the greatest opportunity for automation.
The strongest AS/RS business cases are generally built around automating the products that move most frequently.
Both consume storage space within the AS/RS, but only one generates meaningful operational value.
Every time SKU A is automatically retrieved, labor is eliminated and productivity improves. Over the course of a year, those savings accumulate rapidly. SKU B, on the other hand, occupies valuable automated storage capacity while contributing very little to throughput improvement or labor reduction.
Simply put, high-velocity SKUs produce the transactions that justify the investment.

Across the United States, specialty medical practices are under growing financial pressure. The cost of running a practice is rising faster than revenue.
While the discussion around AI in healthcare has mostly focused on its potential to lower costs and increase efficiency, AI can have a meaningful impact on the other side of the ledger: revenue. Prosper AI conducted a study to quantify the revenue opportunity tied to where practices can introduce AI to provide more consistent, reliable care and improve practice economics in the process.
Prosper AI leveraged data from interactions across patients and insurance companies accounting for more than $3 billion in care managed, and combined that data set with specialty-specific data from the Medical Group Management Association (MGMA). Prosper AI then conducted original research, a phone-access study called CallIQ, to assess the current state of patient access, covering approximately 2,000 practices across 29 states; the specialties included dermatology, ophthalmology, gastroenterology, OB-GYN, primary care, and orthopedics.
Our research identifies four actionable levers within practice leaders’ control, representing an estimated annual revenue opportunity of approximately $125,000 per physician.
CAPTURE DEMAND: Convert missed calls to appointments. Even during office hours, 1 in 6 calls go unanswered. Using AI to answer calls and optimize how schedules are filled can generate an average of $44,800 per physician in annual revenue.
RECAPTURE DEMAND: Re-engage existing patients. Only 54 percent of patients due for a follow-up visit return on schedule; 40 percent come back late and 6 percent never return. Proactive outreach with the help of AI to bring these patients back sooner can unlock up to $37,400 in additional revenue per physician.
PROTECT REIMBURSEMENTS: Prevent avoidable denials. Front-end errors, such as billing an inactive insurance plan, skipping a required insurer approval, or misspelling a patient’s name, drive nearly half of claim denials. Accurate benefits checks done using AI in advance of a visit can eliminate avoidable denials and translate into an average of $28,500 a year per physician.
RECOVER REVENUE: Recover the patient responsibility. Patients now pay 36 percent of the cost of their care, and nearly 8 percent of what they owe goes unpaid.
